October 24, 1940
TAIRIKU SHIMPO

UNOFFICIAL APPOINTMENT OF CHEN KUNG-PO
AS MAYOR OF SHANGHAI

After the decision to appoint Mr. Chen
Kung-po, Minister of the Legislative Yuan, as the new
Mayor of Shanghai in order to reform the administration
of the City Government and deal with questions regarding
the Foreign Settlements, the Nanking Government has since
been seeking understanding with the Japanese and the
Chinese circles concerned on this point.

As the understanding was reached and
Mr. Chen Kung-po himself accepted the offer, his appointment
as the new Mayor of Shanghai has become definite and
an official announcement is expected to be made in the
near future.

Upon the assumption of the new post,
Mr. Chen Kung-po will resign from the Ministry of the
Legislative Yuan. As Secretary-General of the Shanghai
City Government, Mr. Hsu who is now in Peking will be
selected to assist Mr. Chen. Mr. Soo Hsi-wen, who has
been temporarily acting as Mayor of Shanghai since the
death of Mr. Fu Siao-en, is to be transferred to an
important post in the Nanking Government.

（手写签名）
（批：Q 2/10）

1940年10月24日
《大陆新报》

陈公博非正式受任为上海市长

在决定任命立法院部长陈公博先生为新任上海市长，以改革市政府行政并处理有关外国租界的问题后，南京政府一直在就此事寻求与日本及相关中方人士达成谅解。

随着谅解达成且陈公博先生本人接受了这一提议，其出任新任上海市长的任命已确定，预计不久将发布官方公告。

陈公博先生就任新职后，将辞去立法院部长职务。现任在上海市政府担任秘书长的徐先生（目前在北京）将被选中协助陈先生。自傅筱庵先生去世后一直暂代上海市长的苏希文先生，将被调往南京政府担任重要职务。

（手写签名）
（批：Q 2/10）

CONFIDENTIAL
October 27, 1941.

Japanese Military Police - activities in Western District

The Japanese Military Police continues searching
pedestrians intermittently in the Western District, O.O.L.
During the morning of October 26, a party of five uniformed
Japanese gendarmes and several Japanese in plain clothes
searched pedestrians in the vicinity of Jessfield and
Brenan Roads. They were also observed taking away from
newspaper vendors the pro-Chungking papers consisting of
the Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National
Herald, Sin Wan Pao and the Shun Pao.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH 27 OCT 1941）

日本宪兵——在西区活动

日本宪兵继续在越界筑路区域（O.O.L.）的西区间歇性搜查行人。10月26日上午，一队五名身着制服的日本宪兵和几名便衣日本人在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）和布伦南路（Brenan Road）附近搜查行人。他们还被观察到从报贩手中没收亲重庆方面的报纸，包括《正言报》、《中美日报》、《国民新闻》、《新晚报》和《申报》。

SUBJECT: City Government Police Bureau - to
remove to the Shanghai Second Middle
School on Loh Kia Pang Road (陸家
浜路), Nantao.

（印：URGENT）

With reference to the attached newspaper
translation from the "Tairiku Shimpo" dated July 16,
1941, to the effect that the Police Headquarters
of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau will
remove from the Civic Centre, Kiangwan, to the former
site of the Shanghai Second Middle School (上海第二
中學), on Loh Kia Pang Road, Nantao, enquiries show
that this is a temporary measure decided upon by
Col. Loo Ying, Commissioner of the City Government
Police Bureau, in order to facilitate the better
working of the Bureau. The offices will again remove
from the said address to the former site of the
Public Safety Bureau on Boong Lai Road, Nantao, in
the middle of September, this year, after the
withdrawal of the Japanese Gendarmerie from the
Public Safety Bureau in question.

In connection with this matter, it has
been decided by the Police Bureau that the removal
will take place on July 18th till July 21st and that
15 trucks of the Ningpo Household Removal Company
(寧波搬場公司) have been hired for this purpose.
Three removals are scheduled to take place daily, the
first leaving the Civic Centre, Kiangwan, at 9 a.m.
(reaching the Garden Bridge in about 20 or 30 minutes),
second at 12 noon and the third at 3 p.m.

D.D.A.

page_data.en:
May 30, 1941.

Japanese Military Police - distribution
of handbills.

During the morning of May 30, a party of
twelve Japanese Military Police proceeded in a motor
truck along roads in the extra-Settlement roads of
the Western District and occasionally conducted
searches of pedestrians. They also distributed
copies of a handbill, of which the following is a
translation :-

" The gendarmerie is responsible for the
maintenance of peace and order in the Western
District. With the cooperation of the residents,
the situation in the area has been quiet. In
order to afford good protection to the residents,
the Military Police detail members to conduct
searches from time to time for the purpose of
eliminating unruly elements. It is hoped that
the residents will render us assistance without
misunderstanding."

Western District Japanese
Military Police ".
page_data.zh:
1941年5月30日。

日本宪兵 - 分发传单。

5月30日上午，一队十二名日本宪兵乘坐一辆机动卡车，沿西区越界筑路区域的道路行驶，并不时对行人进行搜查。他们还分发了一种传单的副本，译文如下：

“宪兵队负责维持西区的和平与秩序。在居民的配合下，该地区局势平静。为了给居民提供良好的保护，宪兵队派遣成员不时进行搜查，以清除不法分子。希望居民们能予以协助，不要产生误解。”

西区日本
宪兵队”。

5月30日上午，一队十二名日本宪兵乘坐一辆机动卡车，沿西区越界筑路区域的道路行驶，并不时对行人进行搜查。他们还分发了一种传单的副本，译文如下：

“宪兵队负责维持西区的和平与秩序。在居民的配合下，该地区局势平静。为了给居民提供良好的保护，宪兵队派遣成员不时进行搜查，以清除不法分子。希望居民们能予以协助，不要产生误解。

Unrest now exists among the policemen
the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau owing to
small pay. Constables receive $35 - $38 per month
and sergeants, $40 - $50, which is insufficient to
maintain their livelihood under present conditions.
Upon learning of the unrest, Col. Loo
Ying, Commissioner of Police of the Shanghai City
Government, recently requested the Ministry of Police
at Nanking to authorize an increase in the pay of the
Shanghai City Government Police. On May 10 and 11,
the police officers attached to various branches
informed their respective subordinates that the
Ministry of Police was considering this matter and
that all officers and men should wait patiently for
a settlement.

February 13, 1941.

Anti-Opium Section - recently added to the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau.
---------------------

Following receipt of instructions from
Mayor Chen Kung Po of the Shanghai City Government,
Mr. Loo Ying (盧 英 ), Commissioner of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau has established
a new section in the Police Bureau known as the
"Anti-Opium Section" (戒 烟 科) and appointed
Mr. Zau Chah Zung (邵 介 人 ) as Chief of the Section.
Zau is now busily engaged in making the necessary
arrangements and regulations etc. appertaining thereto
which will be published in due course.

It is reported that the Anti-Opium Section
will, despite its title, conduct the public sale of
opium when established and will institute the
registration and licensing of opium addicts which,
it is expected, will be put into force in three months.

A Public Health Bureau (衛 生 局 ) has
been recently established by the Shanghai City
Government. Mr. Yuen Chu Van (袁 矩 範 ) has been
appointed as Officer-In-Charge. - Mr. Yuen has already
assumed office.
page_data.zh:
1941年2月13日。

禁烟科 - 最近增设于上海市政府警察局。
---------------------

奉上海市政府市长陈公博之命，上海市政府警察局局长卢英（盧 英）先生在警察局内设立了一个名为“禁烟科”的新部门，并任命邵介人（Zau Chah Zung）为该科科长。邵目前正忙于制定相关的必要安排和规章等，这些内容将在适当时候公布。

据报，禁烟科尽管名义如此，但在成立后将进行鸦片的公开销售，并将实施鸦片瘾君子的登记和许可制度，预计该制度将在三个月内生效。

上海市政府最近成立了一个卫生局（衛 生 局）。袁矩範（Yuen Chu Van）先生被任命为主管官员。袁先生已经就职。

City Government Police Bureau orders suppression of
activities by idlers in Nantao.

With reference to the attached translation
dated February 7, 1941 to the effect that City Govern-
ment Police Bureau has ordered the suppression of
activities by idlers in Nantao, enquiries show that
all Police stations in Nantao have received, on February
5, the following instructions from Commissioner Loo
Ying of the City Government Police Bureau.
"In order to maintain good peace and order
in Nantao and to curb bad elements from disturbing
shops and residences, all illegal activities should
be strictly prohibited".
No proclamations have as yet been issued for
Public information.
Opium hongs gambling dens and other forms of
vice are still prevalent in the Nantao area.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
CONFIDENTIAL
27 / 1 / 41

Special Branch,
January 24, 1941.

Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government -
Organization, personnel and present strength

The strength of the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau at present is 7501. Classification according
to ranks is as follows .

| Rank | Former strength | Present strength |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Commissioner | 1 | 1 |
| D.C. (Secretary) | 1 | 1 |
| A.C. (Special Deputies) | 2 | 2 |
| Superintendents (chief of the various departments, headquarters) | 5 | 5 |
| Chief Inspectors (Chief of the various corps & officers i/c stations) | 29 | 29 |
| Inspectors (officer i/c stations) | 85 | 85 |
| Sub-Inspectors (officer i/c sub-stations, outposts, & other officers on patrol) | 247 | 247 |
| Sergeants | 780 | 750 |
| Constables | 6,651 | 6,381 |
| | 7,801 | 7,501 |

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER ... (SIGNATURE)）

On instructions from the Ministry of Police,
Nanking, the local Chinese Police Bureau, now known as
the "Shanghai Special Municipality Police Bureau
( 上海特别市警察署 )", will hereafter be known
as "THE SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT POLICE BUREAU ( 上海市
警察署 )" while stations ( 分局 ), sub-stations
( 分駐所 ) and outposts ( 派出所 ) will be named after
the names of the districts or places under their jurisdiction.

上海市政府警察局——
组织、人员及现有编制

上海市政府警察局现有警力为7501人。按职级分类如下：

| 职级 | 原有人数 | 现有人数 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 局长 | 1 | 1 |
| 副局长（秘书） | 1 | 1 |
| 助理局长（特别副官） | 2 | 2 |
| 督察长（各部门主管、总部） | 5 | 5 |
| 总督察（各总队主管及分局主管警官） | 29 | 29 |
| 督察（分局主管警官） | 85 | 85 |
| 副督察（分驻所、派出所主管警官及其他巡逻警官） | 247 | 247 |
| 警长 | 780 | 750 |
| 警员 | 6,651 | 6,381 |
| | 7,801 | 7,501 |

（印：副局长 ... （签名））

奉南京内政部指令，当地中国警察局，现称“上海特别市警察署”，今后将改称为“上海市警察署”，而各分局、分驻所和派出所以其管辖的区或地名命名。

depot, which has hitherto been under the supervision of the

page_data.en:
December 30 , 1940.

Transfer of General Loo Ying, Chief of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, to
the post of Civil Governor of Chekiang Province.

With regard to General Loo Ying's application
to the Nanking Government to accept his resignation,
information from sources in Nanking is that Wang Ching
Wei, Chairman of the Government, rejected the application
and according to information from local City Government
Police circles the whole staff are very pleased because
they think Loo's successor may effect a reorganization
to their detriment.

Previous information showed that Loo Ying did
not wish to give up his post but was compelled by
circumstances to send in his resignation, but in the
meantime requested members of the Nanking Government with
influence to assist him with the executives. In the
middle of this month, Loo bought three armoured cars
which he paid $100,000.00 for and presented one to Chow
Foo Hai, Minister of Finance, one to Ting Muh Tsung,
Minister of Social Affairs, and one to Woo Shih Ngoo,
Chief Secretary of the Shanghai City Government in
order to recompense them for their good offices.

It will be recalled that Loo Ying on November
20, presented Chen Kung Po with an armoured car which
had been purchased at $40,000.00 when Chen assumed office..

According to information from the Ministry of
Police, Nanking, General Loo Ying and Li Shih Chun,
Minister of Police, could not agree with one another
and while Li Shih Chun was in Shanghai, they competed
with one other for influence. Li obtained the post
page_data.zh:
1940年12月30日。

上海市政府警察局局长陆英将军调任浙江省民政厅长。

关于陆英将军向南京政府申请批准其辞职一事，据南京方面消息来源称，政府主席汪精卫驳回了该申请；另据当地市政府警察界消息，全体职员对此甚感欣慰，因为他们认为陆的继任者可能会进行对其不利的改组。

此前的消息显示，陆英并不希望放弃职位，但因形势所迫不得不提交辞呈，同时请求南京政府中有影响力的成员协助其与行政当局交涉。本月月中旬，陆英购买了三辆装甲车，耗资100,000.00美元，并将其中一辆赠予财政部长周佛海，一辆赠予社会部部长丁默邨，一辆赠予上海市政府秘书长吴世午，以酬谢他们的斡旋之功。

需指出的是，陆英曾于11月20日向陈公博赠送了一辆装甲车，该车是在陈就职时以40,000.00美元购得的。

December 30, 1940

Transfer of General Loo Ying, chief of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, to
the post of Civil Governor of Chekiang
Province.

With regard to General Loo Ying's application
to the Nanking Government to accept his resignation,
information from sources in Nanking is that Wang Ching
Wei, Chairman of the Government, rejected the application
and according to information from local City Government
Police circles the whole staff are very pleased because
they think Loo's successor may effect a reorganization
to their detriment.

CONFIDENTIAL
To Sec G

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE * 30 DEC. 1940）

Previous information showed that Loo Ying did
not wish to give up his post but was compelled by
circumstances to send in his resignation, but in the
meantime requested members of the Nanking Government with
influence to assist him with the executives. In the
middle of this month, Loo bought three armoured cars
which he paid $100,000.00 for and presented one to Chow
Foo Hai, Minister of Finance, one to Ting Muh Tsung,
Minister of Social Affairs, and one to Woo Shih Ngoo,
Chief Secretary of the Shanghai City Government in
order to recompense them for their good offices.

It will be recalled that Loo Ying on November
20, presented Chen Kung Po with an armoured car which
had been purchased at $40,000.00 when Chen assumed office.

According to information from the Ministry of
Police, Nanking, General Loo Ying and Li Shih Chun,

Commr. of Police. 30/12/40
Sir:
Inform: S. Burnett
A. C. (Sp. Br.)

Transfer of General Loo Ying, Chief of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, to
the post of Civil Governor of Chekiang
Province.

Further to the previous report on the above
subject dated December 23, 1940, it is learned from
a very reliable source that General Loo Ying tendered
his resignation to the Ministry of Police Administration
in Nanking on December 23.

Since his assumption of office on November 20,
1940, Mr. Chen Kung Po, Mayor of Shanghai, has expressed
dissatisfaction with General Loo Ying because of the
latter's cooperation with the Japanese in giving
protection to the gambling dens in Nantao. In the
early part of the current month, General Loo Ying was
chastised for his inefficiency in his administration of
the Police Training Depot. During the past few days a
proclamation in the name of Mayor Chen Kung Po, which
expressively prohibits public gambling, was observed
posted in the Nantao district and in consequence, Hwo
Wei Lottery suspended on December 24 but gambling dens
continued to operate in the Nantao district.

Commr of Police.
Sir:
Information
A. C. (Sp. Br.)

D. G. (Cr & Sp. Branch)
I asked T. T. Cheyne about this
a day or two ago & he told me
Genl Loo had shown him an order
from the Nanking Govt. refusing to accept
his resignation. This may be untrue,
but so he said, & it may therefore be
wise to enquire further before I pass
on this report.
Commissioner of Police

SECRET
November 5, 1940.
Japanese Military Police in the Western District
------------------

The "Great Western Road Office of the Japanese
Military Police" (大西路日本憲兵隊) which was established
on August 11, 1940 on the premises of the now defunct Honeymoon
Club, a gambling den located next to 42 Great Western Road,
O.O.L., was closed at the beginning of November, 1940. Members
attached to this office, totalling some 50, were transferred -
to that section of the Japanese Military Police situated at the
Tseng Shih Primary School, Fah Hwa Village, off Columbia Road.
The premises vacated will be occupied by the "Western Funeral
Service" (西方儀館), a private business concern.

The following shows the approximate strength of the
Japanese Military Police in the Western District at present :

Western Branch of the Japanese Military             40 members
Police, headquarters, 94 Jessfield Road.

Jessfield Section, Japanese Primary                 10 members
School, Robison Road.

Yu Yuen Road Section, Lane 1136,                    20 members
34 Yu Yuen Road.

Yu Yuen Road Office of the Japanese                 60 members
Military Police, 864 Yu Yuen Road
(formerly New Asia Club).

Section in Tseng Shih Primary School,               70 members
Fah Hwa Village, off Columbia Road.
                                                    ___________
                                                    200 members

It should be noted that the strength of the different sections
has been increased or decreased from time to time depending on
orders from the Japanese Authorities and when they considered
it necessary. Approximately sixty gendarmes out of the above
total were selected from amongst the Japanese troops stationed
in the Toyoda Cotton Mills, 200 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., and
have replaced those transferred to other local branches. They
are at present receiving instruction on the situation as it
affects the Western District and are being taught the Chinese
language at the headquarters of the Western Branch of the Japanese
Military Police, 94 Jessfield Road, by members of the Western
District Police Bureau.

（批：Information）
（批：Sd C G）
（批：US 4 - H-sect 6/11/40）
（印：SHANGHAI MB Nov 6 1940 POLICE）

1940年11月5日。
西区的日本宪兵队
------------------

位于越界筑路区大西路42号旁一家名为“蜜月俱乐部”（Honeymoon Club）的赌博窝点旧址内的“大西路日本宪兵队”，该机构成立于1940年8月11日，已于1940年11月初关闭。隶属于该办事处的约50名成员已被调往哥伦比亚路（Columbia Road）旁法华村曾世小学（Tseng Shih Primary School）的日本宪兵队分部。腾出的房屋将由私营机构“西方仪馆”（Western Funeral Service）占用。

目前西区日本宪兵队的大致兵力如下：

日本宪兵队西部支部，总部，极司菲尔路94号。        40名成员

极司菲尔路分部，罗别根路（Robison Road）日本小学。    10名成员

愚园路分部，愚园路1136弄34号。                      20名成员

日本宪兵队愚园路办事处，愚园路864号
（原新亚俱乐部）。                                  60名成员

哥伦比亚路旁法华村曾世小学分部。                    70名成员
                                                    ___________
                                                    200名成员

需要注意的是，各分部的兵力会根据日本当局的命令及其认为必要的情况不时增减。在上述总数中，约有六十名宪兵是从驻扎在越界筑路区极司菲尔路200号丰田纱厂（Toyoda Cotton Mills）的日军中挑选出来的，他们已替换了被调往其他地方分支机构的人员。目前，他们正在极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队西部支部总部接受有关西区局势的指导，并由西区警察局的成员教授中文。

Sir;

I beg to report information which has come to hand
and verified by D.S.I. Yao Yuen Loong at 13 Jessfield
Road, to the effect that the present "blocade" of Lane
668 Yu Yuen Road and vicinity will probably be lifted
to-day, 29th October, and that a Sub-Station will be
opened in the village of Zee Ka Hoong (金家巷).

Although this information has been verified when
D.S.I. Yao Yuen Loong interviewed Inspector Pu Kuh Tsoong
(巫克忠) at 13 Jessfield Road during afternoon of Oct.
28th, it has not been ascertained the number of men to
be installed in the new Sub-Station.

I am, Sir,

John Cahy

City Government Police in the Western District - Census.

of the Shanghai City Government, the Western
District Police Bureau has notified the different
sub-stations under its control to conduct a
census in the districts within their jurisdiction
commencing from October 15th, 1940. This order
is believed to have been issued in consequence of
the assassination of Mayor Foo Siao An.

SECRET

October 13, 1940.

Japanese Gendarmerie and City Government
Police in the Western District - activities

Following the assassination of Mayor FU SIAO
AN which took place on October 11, the Japanese
Gendarmerie and the City Government Police have
been instructed to intensify their efforts to
arrest terrorists. They have been ordered to
spare no effort in an endeavour to trace the culprit
responsible for the assassination of the Mayor.
In consequence of this order, the Japanese
Military Police and the Chinese Government Police
posted in the Western District, have been religiously
searching pedestrians and vehicles using the extra-
Settlement roads area.

（批：Vio 13/10）

西区的日本宪兵队和市政府警察 - 活动

继10月11日傅筱庵（FU SIAO AN）市长遇刺后，日本宪兵队和市政府警察已接到指示，加紧逮捕恐怖分子。他们奉命不遗余力地追查对市长遇刺负责的凶手。因此，部署在西区的日本宪兵队和中国政府警察一直在戒严式地搜查使用越界筑路区域的行人和车辆。

（批：Vio 10月13日）

Japanese Gendarmes & S.C.G.P.B. Search Parties

At 1:18 p.m. 11.10.40., C.P.S. 1062 reported that
Japanese Gendarmes and members of the S.C.G.P.Bureau were
operating search parties on Robison Road, O.O.L.
    Observation was kept and at the junction of
Robison and Kiaochow Roads was a party of two Japanese
Gendarmes armed with pistols (in their holsters) and an
unarmed member of the S.C.G.P.Bureau. Within fifty
yards of this party was another of three armed Gendarmes
and three men of the S.C.G.P.Bureau. They were searching
pedestrians, cyclists and persons alighting from public
conveyances. The work of the parties on Robison Road

日本宪兵与上海市公安局搜查队在越界筑路道路上行动。

1940年10月11日下午1:18，中央巡逻站1062号报告称，日本宪兵和上海市公安局成员正在越界筑路区的罗别根路上开展搜查队行动。
    进行了观察，在罗别根路与胶州路的交界处，有一组由两名携带手枪（在枪套中）的日本宪兵和一名未武装的上海市公安局成员组成的小队。在该小队五十码范围内，还有另一组由三名武装宪兵和三名上海市公安局人员组成的小队。他们正在搜查行人、骑自行车的人以及从公共交通工具上下车的人员。在越界筑路区罗别根路上的小队工作是间歇性的，并与在中国领土道路外的搜查相结合。最后一次在道路上看到他们是在下午3:55。

(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 11 OCT. 1940 COMMANDANT)

According to information received, some fifty
members of the Japanese Military Police have been
transferred from the headquarters at North Szechuen
Road to the Western District. They have been distributed
between the Western Branch of the Japanese Military
Police, 94 Jessfield Road and its sub-offices in the
Western District. The total strength of the Japanese
Military Police in the Western District is now in the
neighbourhood of 220 men.

Some fifty Japanese gendarmes hitherto
employed in the Western district have been detached to
perform special duty which includes the securing of
information regarding the activities of anti-Japanese
and anti-Wang Ching Wei elements and also that of
criminals in that area. They will wear either foreign
or Chinese dress and have been selected because of
their proficiency in the mandarin and local dialect,
also their knowledge of the situation in the Western
District.

C. Crawford
D. I.

据收到的情报，约五十名日本宪兵已从四川北路总部调往西区。他们被分配至位于极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队西区分部及其在西区各分驻所。目前，日本宪兵队在西区的总兵力约为220人。

此前在西区服役的约五十名日本宪兵已被抽调执行特殊任务，包括搜集有关反日分子及反汪精卫分子活动的情报，以及该地区罪犯的活动情况。他们将穿着西式或中式服装，并因其精通普通话和当地方言，以及对西区局势的了解而被选中。

REPORT
Date September 21, 1940.

Subject Reorganization of the Police Reserve Unit of the Shanghai City
Government Police Bureau.

Made by D.I. Fan Lien-pih, Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan.

Vide Sp. Br.
Report dated
12/9/39.
MC

General Loo Ying, Commissioner of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, submitted,
during July, 1940, an application to the Minister
of Police Administration of the New Central
Government, on the subject of an "increase in
police strength" up to 10,000, in view of the local
tense situation, but the application was refused.
He, however, subsequently approached the Shanghai
Special Service Authorities, for assistance, who
authorized him to reorganize the Police Reserve
Unit into the Police Main Corps (警察總隊) by
the middle of September 1940.

The new Police Main Corps now includes the
full strength of Police Reserve Unit hitherto
stationed in the Western District (648) and that of
the Nanhwei Armed Police Corps (756) which was
formerly under the command of Cheng Miao Keng
(張根). The Police Main Corps consists of
four companies, each company controls 3 sections,
each section having a strength of 108 men, with
the exception of the 4th company which independently
operates 4 sections because of its being over
strength.

General Loo Ying assumed the post of Chief
of the Main Corps and Tsung Zau Pih (曾兆壁) was
appointed to act as his deputy.

Detailed particulars are given hereunder.

（印：23 SEP 1940）

上海市政府警察局局长陆英（Loo Ying）将军于1940年7月间，鉴于当地局势紧张，向新中央政府警政部部长提交了一份关于“增加警力”至10,000人的申请，但该申请被拒绝。然而，他随后向上海特务机关寻求协助，该机关授权他在1940年9月中旬前将警察后备队改组为警察总队（警察總隊）。

新的警察总队目前包括此前驻扎在西区的全部警察后备队人员（648人）以及原由张妙根（Cheng Miao Keng，音译：张根）指挥的南汇武装警察大队（756人）的全部人员。警察总队由四个连组成，每个连管辖3个排，每个排编制为108人，但第四连因超编而独立运作4个排。

陆英将军担任总队长，曾兆壁（Tsung Zau Pih）被任命为其副手。

详细情况如下所述。

Chang Miao Keng was formerly a guerrilla captain in Nanhwei but later was appointed "Commander of the Nanhwei Anti-Communist Self Defence Corps" by the Japanese Military Authorities. His unit was reorganized into the Nanhwei Armed Police Corps in November, 1939, by order of General Loo Ying. In fact, General Loo Ying then had no influence whatsoever over the Armed Corps because the Japanese Military were directing its functions.

Furthermore, Chang Miao Keng was arrested and detained by the Japanese Special Service Section, on 8/12/39, owing to a quarrel over the collection of taxes. During his detention, the Corps affairs were taken over by his deputy Liu Tih Zung.

Hereafter the Nanhwei Armed Police Corps will be completely under the command of General Loo Ying.

Subject Persons in possession of Licenced Fire Arms arrested
by Japanese Gendarmerie Search Party.

Made by S.I. Wilcox Forwarded by (签名：J Mc Farlane)

Sir,
At 6.05 p.m. 5-9-40, a telephone message was
received from the Japanese Gendarmerie requesting the
services of an Interpreter on Yu Yuen Road near Tifeng
Road.

The undersigned, S.I. Li Hsu Fa and F.S. 696
Yoshino attended and ascertained that about six members
of the Japanese Gendarmerie, whilst operating a search
party on Yu Yuen Road, a few yards West of Tifeng Road,
had stopped private M/car Lic. No.10459 and found the
owner Yih Sih Soong (葉雪松) manager of the Central
China Daily news, 303 Honan Road, in possession of
revolver S.M.P. No. Y 7057, permit No.2955, and his
bodyguard Liu Kyung Chwang (刘金章) age 36, in
possession of revolver S.M.P. No. Y 6891, permit No.
A 1444.

The Gendarmes were questioning the two men in
a shop at 341 Yu Yuen Road on arrival of police.

Whilst Police were explaining that these two
Firearms were licenced by the S.M.C. and everything
was quite in order, two plain clothes Japanese appeared
on the scene and insisted on taking the two Chinese
and the Firearms and M/car, Lic. No.10459, to the
Gendarmerie Headquarter at 94 Jessfield, which they
did assisted by the uniform members of the Gendarme.

The Chauffeur remained in the M/car.

(印：REGISTRY DATE 11 9 40)

(签名：John Coughlan)

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

(签名：W B Wilcox)

下述签署人、巡官李旭发（Li Hsu Fa，音译）和警员696号吉野（Yoshino）前往现场，查明约六名日本宪兵队员在愚园路提丰路以西几码处执行搜查任务时，拦停了牌照号为10459的私人机动车，发现车主叶雪松（Yih Sih Soong），河南路303号《华中日报》经理，持有工部局警务处编号Y 7057的手枪，许可证号2955；其保镖刘金章（Liu Kyung Chwang），36岁，持有工部局警务处编号Y 6891的手枪，许可证号A 1444。

警察到达时，宪兵正在愚园路341号的一家商店里审问这两人。

当警方解释这两支枪械已由工部局颁发执照，一切手续合规时，两名便衣日本人出现在现场，坚持要将两名中国人、枪械以及牌照号为10459的机动车带往极司菲尔路94号的宪兵队总部，身穿制服的宪兵队员协助他们完成了这一行动。

司机留在车内。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date September 4, 1940.
Subject Japanese Military Police establish office on Yu Yuen Road.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

A "Yu Yuen Road Office of the Japanese Military Police" (愚園路日本憲兵隊) was established on September 3, 1940 at 864 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L. The premises were formerly occupied by the "New Asia Club" also known as the Broadway Club, a gambling den which closed at the end of July, 1940. Occupation by the Japanese Military Police took place during the early morning of September 3. This office consists of some 50 members in uniform, all being Japanese military police armed with pistols and rifles. One gendarme armed with a rifle is posted outside the entrance to the office. They have been observed communicating with the "Great Western Road Office of the Japanese Military Police", premises of which are located next to 42 Great Western Road.

It is also known that the premises vacated by the "Zao Foong Club" also known as the "101 Club", another gambling den situated on Yu Yuen Road, opposite the Jessfield Park, O.O.L., which closed at the end of July, 1940, are in the course of being repaired. According to information obtained, this house will also be taken over by the Japanese Military Police, after repairs will have been complete.

D. C.(Special Branch).
D. S. I.

事由 日本宪兵队在愚园路设立办事处。
由副督察长洛根呈报并转呈

“愚园路日本宪兵队办事处”（愚園路日本憲兵隊）于1940年9月3日在越界筑路区愚园路864号成立。该处所原为“新亚俱乐部”（New Asia Club），又称百老汇俱乐部（Broadway Club），是一家赌博窝点，已于1940年7月底关闭。日本宪兵队于9月3日凌晨进驻。该办事处由约50名身着制服的人员组成，均为配备手枪和步枪的日本宪兵。一名持步枪的宪兵守卫在办事处入口处。有人观察到他们与“大西路日本宪兵队办事处”进行联络，后者位于大西路42号旁。

另悉，位于越界筑路区愚园路、极司菲尔公园对面，原为“兆丰俱乐部”（Zao Foong Club，音译），又称“101俱乐部”的另一家赌博窝点，已于1940年7月底关闭，其腾空的房屋正在修缮中。据获知的信息，该房屋在修缮完成后也将被日本宪兵队接管。

助理处长（特别处）。

Subject Organization of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

The Shanghai City Government Police Bureau is under the direct control of Mayor Fu Siao En as far as police functioning is concerned, but matters relating to organization, training, treatment and personnel etc., are subject to the direction of the Ministry of Police Administration of the new Central Government at Nanking, the Minister being Chow Fu Hai (周佛海). Prior to the establishment of the Ministry of Police Administration at the end of March, 1940, Chen Chun (陳群), Minister of Interior, exercised the control now vested in Chow Fu Hai.

A chart showing the organization of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau is attached hereto. The organization and strength of the bureau is reported on by this Section from time to time.

Main Corps ( 水上警察隊 ) which is attached to the

隶属于上海市政府警察局的水上警察总队（River Police Main Corps，中文：水上警察队）于1940年5月重组为现在的水上警察组（River Police Section），其警力原为350人，现已增至407人。水上警察组总部仍设在浦东东昌路码头，并在黄浦江和苏州河沿线的不同地点设立了七个分组。（见附件列表）。这支水上警察是独立的，并且

page_data.en:
- 2 -

distinct from the Customs River Police and only operates
in the creeks and waterways away from the Whangpoo and
outside the International Settlement and French Concession limits.

The Hwansha and Pei Tsai Police Bureaux, Pootung,
have been abolished and the officers and men attached
thereto have been transferred to other units. Of the
original 64 officers and men of the Hwansha Police Bureau,
57 were transferred to the River Police Section, and the
remaining 7 to the Nanhwei Police Bureau. The Hwansha
area has now been placed under the jurisdiction of the
Nanhwei Police Bureau.

The Pei Tsai area is now subject to the
jurisdiction of the Yang Sz Police Bureau and the 66
officers and men formerly attached to the now defunct
Pei Tsai Police Bureau are now attached to the Yang Sz
Police Bureau.

and bureaux of the Shanghai City Government Police,
together with their locations and present strength is

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 20 FEB. 1940）
C. 19/2.

With regard to the quantity of rice for free
distribution by the Western District Police Bureau and
the donor thereof, enquiries ascertain that a
total of 2,000 piculs of rice were recently allotted
to the Western District Police Bureau by the
"Shanghai City Government" for distribution to the
poor. However, only some 250 piculs were issued on
February 15 and 16, 1940 and there is no prospect of
the remaining 1750 piculs being distributed. The
latter quantity, it is presumed, will be sold to
the staff employees and constables of the bureau at
some $19.00 per picul.

Most of the rice in question came from Wuhu
and was purchased by the "Shanghai City Government"
at some $16.00 per picul for the avowed object
of relieving the poor people in view of the high
cost of the cereal while a small part of it was
solicited by the organ from rice merchants in the
interior for similar purposes.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.

A. C. (Special Branch).

关于西区警察局免费分发的大米数量及其捐赠者，经查询查明，“上海市政府”最近拨给西区警察局共计2000担大米，用于向穷人分发。然而，在1940年2月15日和16日仅发放了约250担，其余1750担预计不会进行分发。据推测，后一部分大米将以每担约19.00元的价格出售给该局的职员雇员和巡捕。

上述大部分大米来自芜湖，由“上海市政府”以每担约16.00元的价格购买，公开宣称的目的是鉴于粮价高昂而救济贫民，另有一小部分是该机构向内地米商募集用于类似目的。

廖仲坚
副侦探督察

S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
Date: February 17, 1940.
Subject. Western District Police Bureau - distribution of free rice to
the poor.
Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

Copy to D.O.'B'

Between 9 a.m. and 11 a.m. February 15 and 16, 1940
the various sub-stations under the Western District
Police Bureau of the "Shanghai City Government"
situated in the extra-Settlement roads in the
Western District distributed free rice tickets to
the poor people in the Western District, O.O.L.,
who were in possession of "residence certificates."
Each ticket entitles the holder to .02 of a "Zar"
of rice to be obtained from a rice shop situated at
House 16, Dah Kwei Li (大桂里), King Sz Doo Miao,
off Connaught Road, O.O.L.. However, owing to
crowding during the distribution of rice tickets,
the Bureau gave instructions that the work be suspended
from to-day pending re-arrangements.

It is reported that the rice distributed by the
Bureau was collected by the "Shanghai City Government"
from the interior and transported to Shanghai without
taxes.

At the request of its officers and senior
clerical staff employees, the "Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau" has agreed to supply each of them with
one picul of rice at the price of $19.40 per picul.
In consequence the constables and other subordinate
officials of the Bureau are at present agitating for
similar treatment.

Liao Chung Chien
D.S.I.

A.C. (Special Branch)

主题. 西区警察局 - 向穷人分发免费大米。
由. 副侦探督察 廖仲坚 制作 经由. 侦探督察 Crawford

抄送 B区警务总监

1940年2月15日和16日上午9时至11时之间，“上海市政府”西区警察局下属位于西区界外马路的各分驻所，向持有“居住证”的西区界外贫困居民免费分发米票。每张米票持有人可凭票从位于界外康纳脱路金司杜庙大桂里16号的一家米店领取0.02“扎”（Zar）大米。然而，由于分发米票期间出现拥挤，该局指示从今天起暂停此项工作，等待重新安排。

据报道，该局分发的大米是由“上海市政府”从内地征集并免税运至上海的。

应其警官和高级文职职员的要求，“上海市公安局”已同意以每担19.40元的价格向他们每人供应一担大米。因此，该局的巡捕和其他下级官员目前正要求享受同等待遇。

廖仲坚
副侦探督察

助理处长（特务科）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch Station
REPORT
Date January 17, 1940.
Subject "Mr. Loo Ying Assaulted by Japanese Sentry" - article in
Chinese-American Daily News.
Made by D.I. Ian Lien Pih Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The report published in the Chinese-
American Daily News of 16-1-40, to the effect that
Mr. Loo Ying, Police Commissioner of the Shanghai
City Government, was assaulted by a Japanese sentry
on the Garden Bridge several days ago, cannot be
confirmed.
Tsang Lai Ching (張蘭慶), Mr. Loo's
chauffeur who is reported by the paper to have been
dismissed in connection with the assault case,
resides with his wife in a front upstairs room
at 334 Route Vinling, French Concession, but he
very seldom returns home. According to his
wife, he is still employed by Mr. Loo Ying and
there is no truth in the newspaper report that
his master was assaulted by a Japanese sentry.
No confirmation can be obtained from official
sources.

Ian Lien-pih
D. I.
A.C. (Special Branch)

(批：Obtain chauffeur's attendance at H.Q.
thro' T.O. as originally directed.

17/1)

撰写人：侦探长 Ian Lien Pih 转呈人：侦探长 Crawford

《中美日报》于1940年1月16日刊登报道，称上海市政府警察局局长卢英先生数日前在外白渡桥遭一名日本哨兵殴打，此事无法证实。
据该报报道，因涉及此殴打案而被解雇的卢先生司机曾来庆 (Tsang Lai Ching)，与其妻居住于法租界万林路334号楼上临街前间，但他极少回家。据其妻称，他仍受雇于卢英先生，且报纸上关于其主人遭日本哨兵殴打的报道不实。
官方渠道亦无法获得证实。

Ian Lien-pih

page_data.en:
January 16, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News:

LOO YING ASSAULTED BY JAPANESE SENTRY

Several days ago, whilst passing over the Garden Bridge in a motor car, Loo Ying (盧英), Commissioner of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, was stopped and ordered to alight for failing to salute the Japanese sentry.

Not knowing why he had been ordered to do this, Loo Ying alighted and made known his position to the sentry. The sentry became angry and stated that as Commissioner of the Police Bureau, he should have saluted him (the sentry). The Japanese then struck the Police Commissioner in the buttock with the butt of his rifle. The blow knocked Loo Ying down to the ground; he did not dare to say another word.

On seeing this, Loo Ying's chauffeur implored the Japanese sentry for mercy. Loo Ying was helped by the chauffeur to the motor car which drove off into the Foreign Settlement.

Loo Ying later blamed the chauffeur for his misadventure and a quarrel ensued. Greatly displeased, Loo Ying, who had not dared to resist a Japanese sentry, immediately dismissed the chauffeur because he could not tolerate hard words from a chauffeur in his employ.

（批：F.A. Try to locate the chauffeur T.O. Ruty. 7/1）
page_data.zh:
1940年1月16日。
晨间译文。

《中美日报》：

卢英遭日本哨兵殴打

数日前，上海市政府警察局局长卢英 (Loo Ying) 乘车经过外白渡桥时，因未向日本哨兵敬礼而被拦下并勒令下车。

卢英不知为何被勒令下车，遂下车向哨兵表明身份。哨兵大怒，称身为警察局局长，理应向他（哨兵）敬礼。随后，该日本人用枪托击打警察局长的臀部。这一击将卢英打倒在地；他不敢再多言半句。

卢英的司机见状，向日本哨兵求情。司机扶卢英上车，车辆随即驶入外国租界。

事后，卢英将此次不幸归咎于司机，双方发生争吵。卢英因不敢反抗日本哨兵而心中不悦，又因无法容忍受雇司机的顶撞，当即解雇了该司机。

（批注：F.A. 尝试通过交通股 locating 司机 Ruty. 1/7）

CONFIDENTIAL

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 1, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. ...
Date January 20, 1940.

Subject. "Shanghai City Government Police". - reported to be strengthened
by 2,000 men.
Made by. D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

(批：S & C G)
(印：RECEIVED 22 JAN. 1940 COMMISSIONER'S OFFT.)

The report published in the China Press and
Tairiku Shimpo of January 17/8, 1940, to the effect
that the Shanghai City Government Police will be
strengthened by 2,000 men, is untrue.

Prior to June, 1939, the strength of the
Shanghai City Government Police was 5,352 and the
monthly expenditure was $250,000. The strength was
increased by 1,000 men during August, 1939, and the
monthly expenditure was raised to $280,000. When
the control of the Shanghai City Government Police
was taken over by the Ministry of Interior of the
"Reformed Government", in September, 1939, Chen
Chun (陳群), the minister, warned the Chief of
the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau against
further increase in strength on the grounds that
the monthly expenditure of $280,000 was already a
heavy burden for the Ministry.

The present strength of the Shanghai City
Government Police is estimated at 6,213.

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.
A. C. (Special Branch).

(批：Copies to
B. M.
Int. Office!
U. S. Cons. Gen.

1939年6月之前，上海市政府警察的人数为5,352人，月支出为250,000元。1939年8月期间，人数增加了1,000人，月支出增至280,000元。1939年9月，当上海市政府警察的控制权移交给“维新政府”内政部时，部长陈群 (Chen Chun) 警告上海市政府警察局局长不要再增加人数，理由是每月280,000元的支出对内政部而言已是沉重负担。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.1, Special Branch....xxxxxx
REPORT    Date...January 6, 19 40.

Subject....Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government - preparation to
import rice from Wuhu.
Made by................................Forwarded by................................

The proposed import of "See Mee" quality rice
direct from Wuhu for the benefit of the sergeants and
constables attached to the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau, has not materialized. Although the
application was approved by Major General Y. Takeshita
of the Japanese Special Service Department, the
transportation of rice from Wuhu to Shanghai cannot
be freely done because of interference by a number of
Japanese organs which function in the Yangtsze Valley
area.

Commissioner Loo Ying ( □□ ), in view of this,
has detailed one of his men to Wuhu to investigate the
rice situation, and to make arrangements accordingly
when this person submits his report.

报告    日期...1940年1月6日。

事由....上海市政府警察局 - 准备从芜湖进口大米。
撰写人................................转呈人................................

为惠及隶属于上海市政府警察局的警长和警员，拟直接从芜湖进口“See Mee”级大米的计划未能实现。尽管该申请已获日本特务机关竹下 (Y. Takeshita) 少将批准，但由于在长江流域活动的多个日本机构的干扰，从芜湖到上海的大米运输无法自由进行。

鉴于此，局长卢英 ( □□ ) 已派遣一名手下前往芜湖调查大米情况，待此人提交报告后，再作相应安排。

Subject (in full). Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government - preparation
to import rice from Wuhu.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

（批：S.C.G）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 3 JAN. 1940）

The proposed import of "See Mee" quality rice
direct from Wuhu for the benefit of the sergeants and
constables attached to the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau, has not materialized. Although the
application was approved by Major General Y. Takeshita
of the Japanese Special Service Department, the
transportation of rice from Wuhu to Shanghai cannot
be freely done because of interference by a number of
Japanese organs which function in the Yangtsze Valley
area.

Commissioner Loo Ying (盧英.), in view of this,
has detailed one of his men to Wuhu to investigate the
rice situation, and to make arrangements accordingly
when this person submits his report.

（框内文字：Commr of Police / S.I. / Jno Robertson / D.C. (Sp. Br)）

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

Date December 12, 19 39.

Subject The Department Chief of the Police Administration of the Reformed
Government arrives at Shanghai.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Dung Tzo Yu (鄧祖禹), the department chief
of the Police Administration of the Ministry of
Interior of the Reformed Government, recently arrived
here from Nanking to inspect the local Chinese police
administration. Accompanied by Loo Ying (盧英), the
commissioner of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai
City Government, and Koh Shao Yi (郭紹儀), chief
of the Detective Squad, Mr. Dung inspected the Police
Headquarters and its subordinate organs including
the Civic Centre Police Bureau, the Pootung Special
Police Reserve Unit, the Police Training Depot and
the River Police Main Corps on December 6. During
the course of inspection, Hu Teh San (胡德山), and
Loo Chih (盧傑), Chief of the Feng Shien and Nanwei
Police Bureau respectively, were found unqualified
to hold their positions because of their lack of
experience. According to the regulations of the
Ministry of Interior, the chief of a district Police
Bureau should have been at least a sub-inspector for
a period of at least three years. It is learned that
as a result of recommendation made by Loo Ying, the
two officers in question, were permitted to remain in
their posts with the rank of acting-chiefs and given
to improve.

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

维新政府内政部警察行政处处长邓祖禹（鄧祖禹）近日从南京抵达此地，视察当地中国警察行政工作。12月6日，邓先生在上海市公安局局长卢英（盧英）和侦缉队队长郭绍仪（郭紹儀）的陪同下，视察了警察总局及其下属机构，包括市中心区警察局、浦东特别警察后备队、警察训练所和水上警察总队。在视察过程中，发现奉贤和南汇警察局局长胡德山（胡德山）和卢杰（盧傑）分别因缺乏经验而不称职。根据内政部规定，区警察局局长应至少担任副巡官职务满三年。据悉，经卢英推荐，这两名官员被允许以代理局长的身份留任，并予以改进机会。

潘连璧
巡官

The chief of the Shanghai City Government
Western District Police Bureau is reported to have
recently received a confidential order which includes
the following points :-

1) To arrest members of the "Police" or "Defence Forces"
who attempt to obstruct the activities of the
Shanghai City Government Authorities in the
extra-Settlement Roads area in the Western
District.

2) To resist at once in self defence when interfered
with by members of the "Police" or "Defence Forces".

3) To adopt a hostile attitude towards the "Police"
and "Defence Forces".

4) Men on sentry and post duty are strictly prohibited
from retreating during incidents with the
"Police" or "Defence Forces" irrespective of
consequences.

5) Officers and policemen of the Western District
Police Bureau should endeavour to persuade
the "Police" to join the Shanghai City
Government Police.

6) Whenever an opportunity avails itself, the outdoor
staff should insult and find fault with foreign
nationals with the exception of Japanese,
Germans and Italians.

Upon receipt of this confidential order, the
Chief of the Western District Police Bureau has
instructed his subordinates to act accordingly.

Certified True Copy.

J. F. Lovell
JM.

据报，上海市政府西区警察局局长最近收到一份密令，其中包括以下几点：-

1) 逮捕试图在西区越界筑路区域阻碍上海市政府当局活动的“警察”或“防卫队”成员。

2) 当受到“警察”或“防卫队”成员干扰时，立即进行自卫抵抗。

3) 对“警察”和“防卫队”采取敌对态度。

4) 执勤哨兵和岗位人员在与“警察”或“防卫队”发生事件期间，严禁撤退，无论后果如何。

5) 西区警察局的警官和警员应努力劝说“警察”加入上海市政府警察队伍。

6) 一旦有机会，外勤人员应侮辱和挑剔外国人，但日本人、德国人和意大利人除外。

收到此密令后，西区警察局局长已指示其下属照此执行。

认证副本属实。

J. F. Lovell
JM.

With reference to the attached extract from
the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury dated 27/11/39
and report of Bubbling Well Station dated 24/11/39
on desertion by members of the "Shanghai City Govern-
ment" Police in the Western District, discreet en-
quiries ascertain that up to the present some twenty
constables attached to the Special Reserve Unit
stationed in the Western District principally in Fah
Hwa Village have deserted their employment. In
almost all these cases dissatisfaction with their
treatment has been found to be the cause.

The majority of the constables attached to the
Special Reserve Unit of the "Shanghai City Government"
Police are ex-soldiers or ex-members of local militia

this sum they are required to pay $8.00 for food, thus
their net income is only $8.00 per mensem.

Possibly due to shortage of men, they are required
to work continuously day and night. They are divided
into three shifts. Each shift does three hours on duty
and six hours off.

In general, these constables joined the "Shanghai
City Government" Police not for the pay but in the

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

NOV 22 1939

Ta Tao Police
Unit Weakened
By Desertions

Many Abandon Service
Guns, Caps To Quit
Japanese Masters

FOREIGNER FINDS
ABANDONED RIFLE

Small Pay, ‘Dangerous’
Duty Said Causing
General Unrest

Fed to the back teeth which
they are having to perform for
their Japanese masters in the bad-
lands area and particularly on
Shanghai Municipal Council roads,
many desertions in the ranks of
the Ta Tao police have taken
place recently.

Made to stand at street corners
and control traffic, clad in dingy
and ill-cut uniforms, the Ta Tao
police realize that they cut no
figure beside the smartly clad
Chinese members of the SMC.
Moreover, their $16 a month and
bad living accommodation is not a
patch on the conditions of ser-
vice of an SMP Chinese con-
stable.

Eight This Week

This week there have been no
less than eight desertions.

A foreign resident’s report that
he had made a curious discovery
in his garden today is clear evid-
ence of these desertions.

Mr. H. Kliene, living at 3 Lane
310 Yennling Road, looked out into
his garden when he arose at 6.30
a.m. today, and saw a rifle and
a cap. A little later, when he had
dressed, he went out carefully ex-
amined his find. The rifle had
three rounds of ammunition in it.
The cap was that of a Ta Tao
policeman.

Not Enough Pay

Chinese reports say that hun-
dreds of the Ta Tao men are de-
serting. Their pay is not enough for
the dirty work they have to do
and in addition they may have
to face crack shots of the SMP,
some of them armed with sub-
machineguns.

It is also pointed out that most
of the Ta Tao police officers were
recruited from war prison camps.
The Chinese war prisoners, after
due training in Nanking and other
parts of the occupied area, are
distributed among the cities for
police duties and also for service
in the so-called “Pacification
Army.”

1939年11月22日

大道警察部队
因逃兵而削弱

多人弃职
缴还枪支、帽徽以脱离
日本主子的控制

外国人发现
被遗弃的步枪

低薪、“危险”
任务据称引发
普遍不满

对于不得不在不良地区、特别是在上海工部局道路上为其日本主子执行的任务，他们已感到极度厌恶，近期大道警察队伍中发生了多起开小差事件。

大道警察身着肮脏且剪裁不合身的制服，被迫站在街角指挥交通，他们意识到自己与着装整齐的工部局华籍警员相比相形见绌。此外，他们每月16元的薪水及恶劣的居住条件，远不及工部局华籍巡捕的服务条件。

本周八人

本周至少有八人开小差。

一位外籍居民报告称，他今天在其花园里有了一个奇怪的发现，这清楚地证明了这些逃兵事件的存在。

住在延龄路310弄3号的 H. Kliene 先生，今天早上6点30分起床时向花园望去，看到了一支步枪和一顶帽子。稍后，当他穿好衣服后，便出去仔细检查了他的发现。步枪内装有三发子弹。那顶帽子是大道警察的制式帽。

薪水不足

中文报道指出，数百名大道警察正在逃离。他们的薪水不足以补偿他们所从事的肮脏工作，此外，他们还必须面对工部局神枪手的威胁，其中一些人配备有冲锋枪。

还有人指出，大多数大道警官是从战俘营招募的。中国战俘在南京及占领区其他地方接受适当训练后，被分发到各城市担任警察职务，并在所谓的“绥靖军”中服役。

Subject. Information concerning desertion of Shanghai City
Government Special Police attached to West Fah Wah
Sub Station.
Made by Det. Inspector Tabrum Forwarded by [签名]
Inspector i/c.

It has come to notice that during the past few days
several members of the Shanghai City Government Special
Police, attached to the West Fah Wah Sub Station, have
deserted. They returned their equipment to Inspector
Tsang Vung Jih (张文傑) and also expressed their
dissatisfaction to him. The personal of this particular
Sub Station were formerly soldiers who were taken
prisoners by the Japanese Military, and trained for
police duties. These men have not been satisfied with
their conditions (they are paid about $16.00 per month,
and deductions are made for food, etc.) and recently, 10
of them applied for leave, and failed to return to duty.
One member, detailed for the protection of
transportation of opium, deserted his post on 20-11-39,
and took his Mauser pistol and equipment with him.

R. J. Tabrum

November 22, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Pao, Shun Pao, Hwa Pao:

JAPANESE REMOVING S.M.C. BARRICADES IN WESTERN
DISTRICT

With a view to maintaining peace and order,
the S.M.C., after the outbreak of hostilities on August 13,
-1937, closed with barbed wire barricades all unnecessary
passages and alleyways along the extra-Settlement roads
in the Western District, especially on the roads adjacent
to the Settlement area. Later, conditions in the
outlying roads area in the Western District became very
bad as a result of the presence of puppet police and
troops. Consequently, the authorities of the Settlement
put up more barbed wire barricades along the districts
wherein these elements are to be found.
Now, at a time that the Settlement authorities
are making preparations to enforce winter precautions,
the Japanese and the puppet authorities during the past
few days have been removing the barricades along Amherst
Avenue, Great Western Road and Tunsin Road without first
securing the approval of the Council. In some places
exits have been opened. The barricades erected at the
south end of Avenue Haig adjacent to the Settlement and
along Loh Ka Road at Zi Ka Wei and Fah Hwa East Village
have likewise been demolished, while those along Lu Sih
Zah (雷家宅) on Brenan Road, Yu Yuen Road and Zau Ka Zah
(曹家宅) have already been removed.

1939年11月22日。
下午译文。

《大美报》、《申报》、《华报》：

日本人拆除工部局在西区的路障

为了维持治安，自1937年8月13日战事爆发后，工部局用铁丝网路障封闭了西区越界筑路沿线所有不必要的通道和小巷，特别是靠近租界区域的道路。后来，由于伪警察和伪军的存在，西区外围道路地区的状况变得非常糟糕。因此，租界当局在这些势力出现的地区设立了更多的铁丝网路障。
现在，正值租界当局准备实施冬季预防措施之际，日本人和伪当局在过去几天里，未经工部局批准，便拆除了沿阿美士德路 (Amherst Avenue)、大西路 (Great Western Road) 和同信路 (Tunsin Road) 的路障。在一些地方开辟了出口。海格路 (Avenue Haig) 南端毗邻租界处以及徐家汇罗家路 (Loh Ka Road) 和法华东路 (Fah Hwa East Village) 沿线的路障也被拆除，而白利南路 (Brenan Road) 上的雷家宅 (Lu Sih Zah)、愚园路 (Yu Yuen Road) 和曹家宅 (Zau Ka Zah) 沿线的路障则已被移除。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao of Oct.25: 26.10.29 (AM)

POLICE BUREAU OFFICIAL DETAINED FOR GIVING OUT
CERTAIN SECRETS

Recently a big affair occurred in the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau in Kiangwan. It was
discovered that certain "secrets" had been divulged by some
"public officer." Loo Ying (盧英), Commissioner of the
Police Bureau, has placed the principal offender under
detention and has kept the matter secret with the result
that even his subordinates know nothing about the affair.
However, according to information from certain
sources, the culprit is one Hsu Chong (許昌), native of
Chinkiang, who was formerly a reporter of the "Sin Shun Pao,"
a Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper. Through his
work, he became acquainted with Shao Chia-jen (邵介人),
Chief Secretary to the Police Commissioner. Through the
introduction of the Chief Secretary, Hsu Chong secured a
post in the Secretariat several months ago.
Recently it was ascertained that certain "secrets"
had been given out by Hsu Chong.
It is learned that Hsu Chong has admitted his
connection with Chinese guerrillas. It is not known how
he will be dealt with.

《华美晚报》10月25日：29年10月26日（上午）

警察局官员因泄露某些机密被拘留

近日，江湾上海市政府警察局发生了一起重大事件。发现某些“机密”被某“公职人员”泄露。警察局局长卢英已将主要肇事者拘留，并对此事保密，以致其下属对此事一无所知。
然而，据某些消息来源透露，罪犯是许昌，镇江人，前日文中文报纸《新顺报》记者。通过工作，他结识了警察局长首席秘书邵介人。通过首席秘书的介绍，许昌于数月前在秘书处谋得一职。
最近查明，某些“机密”是由许昌泄露的。
据悉，许昌已承认与中国游击队有联系。尚不清楚他将受到何种处理。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 1 3 1939

“Ta Tao” Maneuvers
Fail To Materialize
But Guerillas Active

“Ta Tao” police maneuvers, scheduled to have been staged in Japanese controlled areas of the western district yesterday afternoon, were not held as announced, it was learned last night.

The maneuvers, according to an announcement made by the “Ta Tao” police authorities, were to include machine-gun and rifle firing. Residents of the area were asked not to be alarmed. And residents were not alarmed for the simple reason that the “war games” did not materialize.

It is believed that the maneuvers may have been called off because of reported guerilla activity in the Hungjao Airdrome area and at Tsinpu. Japanese tanks and trucks filled with infantry men were rushed off in the direction of Tsinpu on two different occasions yesterday and considerable firing was heard.

Liu

“大淘”演习

据悉，原定昨天下午在西区日控区域举行的“大淘”警察演习未按公告举行。

据“大淘”警察当局公告，演习内容包括机枪和步枪射击。要求该地区居民不要惊慌。居民们并未惊慌，原因很简单，“战争游戏”并未成真。

据信，演习可能因据报道虹桥机场地区和真如地区有游击队活动而被取消。昨天，满载步兵的日本坦克和卡车两次紧急驶向真如方向，并听到大量枪声。

The Western District Police Bureau which removed
from 92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., to Nos. 11 and 13, Jess-

address this morning, November 13, 1939. The former
premises, 92 Jessfield Road, are occupied by some 200
members of the Special Reserve Unit" of the "Shanghai
City Government" Police, who were transported to this
address from Pootung in August and September, 1939.

It is reported that in addition to the 360 members
of the "Special Reserve Unit" stationed in the enclaves, 200
at No. 92 Jessfield Road, and 160 in the Tseng Shih Middle
School, Fah Hwa Village, another 300 are now billeted in
the Toyoda Cotton Mill, No. 200 Jessfield Road, (beyond
the perimeter). Of the latter number, 100 are assigned
to assist the Japanese Military to maintain peace and
order in the area immediately beyond the perimeter, while
the remaining 200 are despatched from time to time into
the enclaves to reinforce the police units there. In
such cases, they invariably enter the enclaves via Chapel
and the San Kwang Dang Bridge which connects Chapel and
Jessfield Area at the loop road behind Jessfield Road,

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

NOV 10 1939

S.M.P. Hampered
In Work in West
Recovery of Part of Bank
Loot Said Frustrated by
"Municipality" Police
SPECIAL TO THE "N.C.D.N."
With the present wave of crime and lawlessness, which is sweeping Shanghai from Yangtzepoo to Jessfield, the police of both the International Settlement and the French Concession are taxed with problems of investigation and apprehension of evil-doers as perhaps never before in the history of the community. In recent months, the western "enclaves"—which are beyond the jurisdiction of the Settlement authorities—particularly have become the breeding ground and shelter of major crime as well as the armoury of some of the worst gangs known to the police.
Inquiries made by the "North-China Daily News" yesterday disclosed the fact that since the beginning of the lawbreakers' Roman holiday, little or no co-operation has been given the Settlement Police by the "Special Municipality" in their effort to track down gangs or individuals sheltering in outside-roads territory. Consequently the police have been unable, time and again, to arrest important criminals whose whereabouts they have ascertained, or to recover stolen property.
Robbers Get $135,000
Eleven Chinese, about half of whom carried pistols, robbed the Kiu Ju Ho Kee Bank, 84 Seward Road, in the Japanese defence sector, of $135,000 on the evening of October 12 last. Subsequently the Settlement Police arrested a number of suspects, some of whom admitted participation in the looting, and recovered a fair portion of the loot, which represented various currencies. These arrests and recoveries were made in the Wayside and Louza districts.
On questioning, some of the prisoners told detectives where about $8,000 more of the plunder was concealed in houses in the Jessfield area. It is understood that the Settlement Police, desiring to verify the prisoners' statement, requested the assistance of the Japanese authorities to search the places mentioned, were referred by the Japanese military to the "Special Municipality" police, who failed to give the necessary assistance.
Officials interviewed yesterday stated that, while the S.M.P. unhesitatingly extend help to other police bodies, including the "Special Municipality" force, little or no co-operation has been given the Settlement Police in their endeavour to bring to justice criminals operating from, or hiding in, the western badlands.

《字林西报》，

1939年11月10日

工部局警务处
在西区工作受阻
据称部分银行劫赃的追回
因“市政府”警察而受挫
《字林西报》专讯
随着犯罪和无法无天的浪潮席卷上海，从杨树浦到极司菲尔路（Jessfield），公共租界和法租界的警方在调查和逮捕罪犯方面所面临的问题，或许是社区历史上前所未有的。近几个月来，位于租界当局管辖范围之外的西部“飞地”，尤其已成为重大犯罪的滋生地和庇护所，以及警方所知一些最恶劣帮派的军火库。
《字林西报》昨日进行的调查显示，自违法者开始肆意妄为以来，“特别市”在租界警方追踪藏匿于越界筑路地区（outside-roads territory）的帮派或个人的努力中，几乎未给予任何合作。因此，警方一再无法逮捕那些已查明下落的重要罪犯，也无法追回被盗财产。

劫匪获赃款13.5万元
去年10月12日晚，11名中国人（其中约一半携带手枪）抢劫了位于日本防区西华德路84号的久聚和记银行（Kiu Ju Ho Kee Bank），劫走13.5万元。随后，工部局警务处逮捕了一些嫌疑人，其中一些人承认参与了抢劫，并追回了相当一部分代表各种货币的赃款。这些逮捕和追缴行动是在威赛德（Wayside）和罗家嘴（Louza）地区进行的。
在审讯中，一些囚犯告诉侦探，另有约8,000元赃款藏在极司菲尔路地区的一些房屋里。据悉，工部局警务处为了核实囚犯的供词，请求日本当局协助搜查上述地点，但被日军转介给“特别市”警察，后者未能提供必要的协助。
昨日接受采访的官员表示，虽然工部局警务处毫不犹豫地向其他警察机构（包括“特别市”警力）提供帮助，但在其致力于将活动于或藏匿于西部混乱地带（western badlands）的罪犯绳之以法的努力中，几乎未得到租界警方的合作。

There are about 300 men of the Police Corps

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :- 4.11.29 (BN)

CITY GOVERNMENT POLICE TO MOVE INTO NEW QUARTERS

Owing to the insufficiency of rooms in the
former premises, the Western District Branch of the City
Government Police Bureau has decided to move its offices
to the premises of Zan's residence, corner of Jessfield
and Tifeng Roads. The refugees formerly living in the
premises have been repatriated and all preparations have
now been completed. Within about five days, all the men
of the Branch Office will attend their offices in the new
premises.

With a view to strengthening the police force
in the area, the Special Municipal authorities will detail
3,000 policemen to garrison the Western District. The
former premises of the Branch Office will be used as their
headquarters.

由于原址房间不足，市政府警察局西区分局决定将其办事处迁至极司菲尔路与地丰路转角处的詹氏住宅。原住在此处的难民已被遣返，所有准备工作现已完成。大约五天内，分局的所有人员将在新址办公。

page_data.en:
TAIRIKU SHIMPO 25·10·39

CHANG MIAO KENG, FORMER CHIEF OF GUERRILLAS IN
POOTUNG, NOW WORKING WITH JAPANESE SOLDIERS

A Chinese officer named Chang
Miao Keng, who carried out vigorous activities in
Pootung district even after the districts had fallen
into Japanese hands, has now turned over a new leaf
and surrendered to the Japanese army.
He has since been engaged
together with Lien Tih Chang and other subordinates
in pacification work against guerrillas, preservation
of peace and order, guarding the Shanghai-Nanking
Railway and protecting military telegraphs and telephones
etc. under the instructions of the Commander of the
Kikuchi Detachment which supplies guards for the
district south of Shanghai.
Being influenced by their
earnest operations and persuasion, more than 1,000
guerrillas have sworn allegiance to our Imperial Forces.
After these men had been
incorporated into the armed police force in Nanhui
District, a marchpast of more than 1,000 men, including
Chang Miao Keng, Chief of the new police force, took
place before Commander Kikuchi on October 23.
Every one of them marched past
with firm determination and showed their passion for
constructing a new China; thus Commander Kikuchi was
moved to admiration.
page_data.zh:
《大陆新报》 1939年10月25日

张妙根，前浦东游击队首领，
现与日军合作

一名名叫张妙根的中国军官，在该地区落入日军手中后，仍在浦东地区进行积极活动，现已改过自新，向日军投降。
此后，他在为上海以南地区提供警卫的菊池支队指挥官的指示下，与连铁长（Lien Tih Chang，音译）及其他下属一起从事针对游击队的绥靖工作、维持治安、守卫沪宁铁路以及保护军用电信电话等。
受到他们真诚行动和劝说的影响，已有1,000多名游击队员宣誓效忠皇军。
在这些人员被编入南汇县的武装警察部队后，包括新警察部队首领张妙根在内的1,000多人于10月23日在菊池指挥官面前进行了阅兵。
每个人都以坚定的决心走过检阅台，展示了他们建设新中国的热情；从而使菊池指挥官深受感动并予以赞赏。

Pao: 21.10.39 (AM)

THE REFUGEES AT JESSFIELD CAMP

The 31st Refugee Camp in Jessfield Road was
established by the Shanghai Refugee Relief Association
on Avenue Edward VII. Following the dispute arising out
of the extra-Settlement roads area question, the Association,
in order to avoid unpleasant experiences, devised ways and
means to remove the camp elsewhere.
Subsequently it was learned that there were
vacant grounds at the Refugee Camp in Tunsin Road, on which
huts for refugees might be erected. Unexpectedly when
Kwei Yien-fang (桂延芳) was making arrangements with the
Association in this connection, the refugee camp in
Jessfield Road was occupied by City Government policemen.
In the summer of this year, two houses were built
to be used as premises for a Refugee Children's School.
At this time of emergency, the Association, apart from
making every effort to undertake the repatriation of refugees,
has to accommodate certain old and weak refugees in the
school premises. As soon as the erection of huts in
Tunsin Road is completed, the removal of these refugees
will take place.

《大美报》、《中美日报》、《申报》、《新闻报》：1939年10月21日（上午版）

极司菲尔路难民营的难民

极司菲尔路的第31难民收容所是由上海难民救济协会在爱多亚路建立的。由于越界筑路区问题引发争端，该协会为避免不愉快经历，设法将难民营迁往他处。
随后获悉，顿思路的难民收容所有空地，可在其上搭建难民棚屋。不料，当桂延芳就此与协会进行安排时，极司菲尔路的难民营已被市政府警察占领。
今年夏季，建造了两栋房屋用作难民儿童学校的校舍。在此紧急时刻，协会除尽力开展难民遣返工作外，还不得不将部分老弱难民安置在校舍内。一旦顿思路的棚屋搭建完毕，这些难民即行迁移。

October 19, 1939.    Morning Translation.

Shun Pao, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News:-
JAPANESE TAKE OVER REFUGEE CAMP IN JESSFIELD ROAD

Building No. 11 Jessfield Road, outside
Settlement limits, was originally used as a club by the
staff of the Hou Yen Ping Coal and Mining Company. After
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, it was
converted into the 31st Refugee Camp.
On the afternoon of September 9 this year, the
Japanese and puppet military occupied the ground floor and
two large rooms belonging to the refugee camp. In addition
they put up sand bags in front of the house and posted
sentries on duty. Barbed wire entanglements were erected
on a piece of vacant ground. Thus the Refugee Camp and
the refugee children's school had to open a side door for
their use. Subsequently, the Japanese occupied two more
rooms as kitchens.
On October 1 the land owner in a notice
to the Refugee Camp announced that as the house is required
by the Consolidated Tax Bureau for use as offices, the
Refugee Camp was asked to vacate the premises by October 15.
The Camp sent a report to the Federation
of Charity Organizations and negotiations were opened with
the land owner but without result.
At 2 p.m. October 17, a Japanese gendarme,
accompanied by over ten policemen of the Shanghai City
Government, arrived at the camp and drove away the 600
refugees. About 200 of these refugees have gone elsewhere,
but the other 400 spent the night in the open air. It is
earnestly hoped that measures will be adopted for the relief
of these refugees.

Precautionary Measures Along Jessfield Road

At 9 a.m. yesterday strict precautionary
measures were adopted along Jessfield Road by armed
policemen of the Shanghai City Government and the Japanese
Special Service Corps. Groups of six armed policemen were
noticed on patrol duty.
According to information secured from a
certain source, the adoption of strict precautionary
measures yesterday morning was due to the assassination
of Zeng Hai-do (程海), a Secretary-Interpreter of the
Political Branch of the French Police.
Policemen of the Shanghai City Government
have been detailed to take a census of the population in
the Western District of Shanghai.

O.T! Leao,
Pnt

1939年10月19日。    晨间译文。

《申报》、《大美报》、《新闻报》、《中美日报》：-
日军接管极司菲尔路难民营

位于租界界限外的极司菲尔路11号建筑，原为厚源平煤矿公司职员俱乐部。中日战事爆发后，该处被改为第31难民收容所。
今年9月9日下午，日军及伪军占领了难民营的一楼及两间大房间。此外，他们在房前堆起沙袋并派哨兵执勤。在一块空地上架设了铁丝网。因此，难民营和难民儿童学校不得不开启一扇侧门供其使用。随后，日军又占用了两个房间作为厨房。
10月1日，地主向难民营发出通知，称因统税局需使用该房屋作为办公处，要求难民营于10月15日前腾空房屋。
难民营向慈善团体联合会提交报告，并与地主展开谈判，但未果。
10月17日下午2时，一名日本宪兵 accompanied by 十余名上海市政府警察抵达难民营，驱散了600名难民。其中约200名难民前往他处，其余400人则在露天过夜。恳切希望采取措施救济这些难民。

极司菲尔路沿线的预防措施

昨日上午9时，上海市政府武装警察和日本特别工作队沿极司菲尔路采取了严格的预防措施。观察到每组六名武装警察在执行巡逻任务。
据某消息来源获悉，昨日上午采取严格预防措施是由于法国警务处政治科秘书兼翻译曾海多（程海）遇刺身亡。
上海市政府警察已受命对上海西区人口进行普查。

O.T! Leao,
Pnt

TAIRIKU SHIHO 25·10·29

CHANG MIAO KENG, FORMER CHIEF OF GUERRILLAS IN
POOTUNG, NOW WORKING WITH JAPANESE SOLDIERS

A Chinese officer named Chang
Miao Keng, who carried out vigorous activities in
Pootung district even after the districts had fallen
into Japanese hands, has now turned over a new leaf
and surrendered to the Japanese army.
He has since been engaged
together with Liou Tih Chang and other subordinates
in pacification work against guerrillas, preservation
of peace and order, guarding the Shanghai-Nanking
Railway and protecting military telegraphs and telephones
etc. under the instructions of the Commander of the
Kikuchi Detachment which supplies guards for the
district south of Shanghai.
Being influenced by their
earnest operations and persuasion, more than 1,000
guerrillas have sworn allegiance to our Imperial Forces.
After these men had been
incorporated into the armed police force in Nanhui
District, a marchpast of more than 1,000 men, including
Chang Miao Keng, Chief of the new police force, took
place before Commander Kikuchi on October 23.
Every one of them marched past
with firm determination and showed their passion for
constructing a new China; thus Commander Kikuchi was
moved to admiration.

（印：COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

《大陆时报》 1939年10月25日

张妙根，前浦东游击队首领，现与日军合作

一位名叫张妙根的中国军官，即使在浦东地区落入日军之手后仍在该地区积极开展活动，现已改邪归正，向日军投降。
此后，他在负责上海以南地区警卫任务的菊池支队长的指令下，与刘铁长及其他下属一起从事肃清游击队、维护治安、守卫沪宁铁路以及保护军用电报电话等工作。
受到他们真诚行动和劝说的影响，已有1000多名游击队员宣誓效忠皇军。
在这些人员被编入南汇区武装警察部队后，包括新警察部队首领张妙根在内的1000多人于10月23日在菊池支队长面前进行了阅兵式。
每个人都以坚定的决心走过检阅台，展示了建设新中国的热情；从而使菊池支队长深受感动并为之赞叹。

（印：总监办公室）

加藤曹长回复称，日本宪兵队仅处理政治案件，鉴于此为刑事案件，日本宪兵队将协助上海市政府警察局，由该局向上海公共租界工部局警务处提供协助。加藤曹长进一步透露，该案将由上海市政府警察局办理，若有人被捕，将由在越界筑路区西区运作的中国法庭审判；此外，由上海公共租界工部局警务处羁押的嫌疑人必须移交给他们，以便带领他们前往涉案房屋，但上海公共租界工部局警务处人员不得进入中国领土。讨论结束后，被告知加藤曹长，关于逮捕通缉犯和追回赃款的进一步谈判

上述决定已通知刑事科副督察长，并指示可在获得由王德林签署、Suwa少佐副署的书面收据的条件下移交囚犯，且囚犯必须于1939年10月17日晚上7时前归还。
Suwa少佐获知上述情况后，起初拒绝签署收据，声称其仅以顾问身份行事；然而，在再次被告知若无收据则不得允许囚犯离开上海公共租界警务处的羁押后，他同意在王德林撰写的收据上副署。

At 5.00 p.m., after receiving the above information three or four detectives of the S.C.G.Police Bureau left the office and proceeded to the above address without taking the prisoner with them to identify Wong Zau Shing which was rather an unusual procedure and this fact was brought to the notice of Major Suwa who made the excuse that if the prisoner was seen by the wanted man and his colleagues they would probably make good their escape.

It is worthy of note that the receipt had not been endorsed by Wong Tuh Ling or Major Suwa at this time.

At 5.45 p.m., S.C.G.Police Bureau detectives returned together with Tsang Ah Doo (□□□), the proprietor of the Lee Yih Gambling Hall, and reported that there was no person named Wong Zau Shing or any person answering the description given by the prisoner employed in the gambling establishment.

The prisoner was questioned in the presence of Tsang Ah Doo and maintained that Wong Zau Shing was employed at one of the gambling tables in his establishment, whereupon, the S.C.G.Police Bureau detectives at 5.50 p.m. after the receipt was signed took the prisoner to the Lee Yih Gambling Hall to identify Wong Zau Shing returning at

Subject Inspection tour of Loo Ying, Police Commissioner of Shanghai
City Government - proposed reorganization of the "Nanhwei
Anti-Communist Self-Defence Corps"

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. G...

At 8.30 a.m. on October 12, 1939, Loo Ying
(盧英), Commissioner of the Shanghai City Govern-
ment Police Bureau, accompanied by a party of sub-
ordinates including Kuo Shao-yi (郭紹儀), Chief
of the Detective Corps, Pao Tse-ying (子英), Chief
of the River Police Main Corps and L. Taketsuchi
(武土蘭), a Japanese advisor, proceeded from
Hongkew to Chowpu, Pootung, where they were received
by Loo Chih (盧傑), Officer-in-charge of the
Nanhwei Branch Police Bureau. The details of the
Nanhwei Branch Police Bureau were inspected by Loo
Ying.

At 11 a.m., an inspection parade of over
700 members of the Nanhwei Anti-Communist Self-Defence
Corps under the command of Chang Miao-keng (張妙根).
was held in Chowpu. - Loo Ying took the salute in
the march past.

It will be noted that the Nanhwei Anti-Com-
munist Self-Defence Corps has a total strength of
over 700 men under Chang Miao-keng and was formed
in the Spring of this year from ex-guerillas operating
in the suburbs of this city who have since surrendered
to the Japanese. It is the intention of the local
Japanese authorities to reorganize this corps into
an armed police unit and to incorporate it into the
strength of the Police Bureau under Loo Ying in order
to further increase the strength of the Police Bureau.

1939年10月12日上午8时30分，上海市政府警察局局长卢英（Loo Ying），在包括侦探总队队长郭绍仪（Kuo Shao-yi）、水上警察总队队长鲍子英（Pao Tse-ying，原文注：子英）以及日本顾问武土兰（L. Taketsuchi）在内的下属陪同下，从虹口前往浦东周浦，受到南汇分局警察局负责人卢杰（Loo Chih）的接待。卢英视察了南汇分局警察局的详细情况。

上午11时，在周浦举行了由张妙根（Chang Miao-keng）指挥的南汇反共自卫团700多名成员的检阅游行。卢英在分列式行进中接受敬礼。

值得注意的是，南汇反共自卫团在张妙根麾下总兵力超过700人，成立于今年春季，成员由此前在该市郊区活动、后向日军投降的前游击队组成。当地日本当局意图将该团重组为武装警察部队，并将其纳入卢英领导的警察局编制，以进一步增加警察局的实力。

Ta Ying Yeh Pao dated October 12 :- 13.10.39 (PM)
MAYOR FU SIAO-EN ATTEMPTS TO REORGANIZE TROOPS IN POOTUNG

The so-called Chinese troops in Pootung are
directly under the control of the Japanese military
authorities and the Pootung Administrative Office have no
control over their activities.
Recently the troops have been collecting
taxes by force. As this will affect the revenue of the
Shanghai City Government, Mayor Fu, who intends to
reorganize these troops into a police unit to be controlled
by Police Headquarters, is endeavouring to secure permission
from the Japanese military authorities. The troops are
unanimously opposed to any reorganization.

《大英夜报》10月12日讯 :- 1939年10月13日（下午）
傅筱庵市长试图重组浦东部队

所谓在浦东的中国军队直接受日本军事当局控制，浦东行政公署对其活动无权管辖。
最近，这些部队一直在强行征税。由于这将影响上海市政府的收入，打算将这些部队重组为由警察总局控制的警察单位的傅市长，正努力争取日本军事当局的许可。这些部队一致反对任何重组。

Sir,

At 12.50 p.m. 28-9-39, the S.C.G.P.B. established a
traffic post at the corner of Robison and Kiaochow Roads
when one of their members, unarmed, commenced directing
traffic.

Representations were immediately made to the
Headquarters of the Italian Marines by telephone when
the following reply from Count Bentivoglio was received.
"The Commander of the Italian Marines will exert his
influence in order to have such man taken away as soon as
possible".

At 3 p.m. even date the man was withdrawn and has
not so far re-appeared.

This corner has never previously been considered a
traffic post by the S.M.P.

September 10, 1939. Morning Translation

Ta Mei Weekly, . Shun Pao; Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American
Daily News:-

JAPANESE SUPPORT CITY GOVERNMENT POLICEMEN AND
INVADE THE EXTRA-SETTLEMENT ROADS AREA

Under the pretext of avoiding untoward
incidents in China, the Japanese have requested the
British and French authorities to withdraw their troops
stationed within the Japanese occupied areas. At a
reception to newspapermen held on the morning of
September 6, the Japanese naval spokesman stated that
necessary steps will be taken in order to have British
soldiers removed from the areas in question, since
diplomatic circles regard the matter as a "problem of
the Settlements". During the past few days, rumours
have been rife to the effect that the Japanese will
seize the Police rights over the extra-Settlement roads
areas by taking advantage of their present opportunity.
Up to yesterday the British and French authorities had
not replied to the Japanese request regarding their
military formations. The Japanese soldiers and
policemen of the Shanghai City Government yesterday
afternoon occupied the refugee camp on Jessfield Road
and posted sentries at the entrance.
Britain and France have wide-spread
interests in the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai whilst
America has expressed her determination to maintain the
present status quo of Shanghai; therefore developments
in this controversy will attract the attention of many
powers.
According to a reporter of the Dah Chung News
Agency (大中社 ) who personally made an investigation
on the scene, it is learned that shortly before 10 a.m.
yesterday, two Japanese officers accompanied by an
interpreter went to the Dzu Lien 31 Branch Refugees Camp
(慈联卅一分会难民收容所) at House No.11 Jessfield Road, and
after holding an inspection of the house upstairs and
downstairs and drawing a sketch map, they left the place.
In all they were on the premises for about 30 minutes.
At 4 p.m. yesterday, about 40 Japanese
soldiers, accompanied by some 20 policemen of the
Shanghai City Government, arrived at the refugee camp
in several trucks and occupied two big rooms, one an
office of the employees of the camp and the other a
living room for the refugees. They also erected a
sand bag wall in front of the gates and installed machine
guns there, whilst vacant ground inside the camp was
surrounded with barbed wires. No inmates or officials
of the Refugee Children Middle School (难童中学 ) were
allowed by the Japanese to go by the front doors but had
to use another door which was temporarily made in the
fence on the north side of Jessfield Road as an exit.

1939年9月10日。晨间译文

《大美周刊》、《申报》、《新闻报》、《中美日报》：-

日本支持市政府警察并侵入越界筑路区域

以避免在中国发生不幸事件为借口，日本要求英法当局撤出驻扎在日本占领区内的军队。在9月6日上午举行的记者招待会上，日本海军发言人表示，鉴于外交界将此视为“租界问题”，将采取必要步骤将英国士兵从相关地区撤出。过去几天，谣言四起，称日本将利用当前机会夺取越界筑路区域的警察权。截至昨日，英法当局尚未就日本的军事部署要求作出答复。昨日下午，日本士兵和上海市政府警察占领了杰斯菲尔德路的难民收容所，并在入口处布置了哨兵。
英国和法国在上海的外国租界拥有广泛的利益，而美国已表示决心维持上海的现状；因此，这一争端的发展将引起许多国家的关注。
据大中社（Dah Chung News Agency）记者实地调查获悉，昨日上午10点前不久，两名日本军官在一名翻译的陪同下前往杰斯菲尔德路11号的慈联卅一分会难民收容所，在对楼房上下进行视察并绘制草图后离开。他们在该处停留了约30分钟。
昨日下午4时，约40名日本士兵在约20名上海市政府警察的陪同下，乘数辆卡车抵达难民收容所，占领了两个大房间，一间是收容所职员的办公室，另一间是难民的起居室。他们还在大门前构筑了沙袋墙并在此安装了机枪，同时用铁丝网围住了收容所内的空地。日本人不允许难民儿童中学（Refugee Children Middle School）的任何住客或官员从前门经过，而是必须使用临时在杰斯菲尔德路北侧围栏上开设的另一扇门作为出口。

page_data.en:
At about 7 p.m. yesterday, a truck carrying
some 30 British soldiers rushed to the spot and on the
pavement opposite the refugee camp mounted a machine gun
facing the City Government-position, thereby causing a
very tense atmosphere. This state of affairs continued
for some time until the British soldiers were ordered to
withdraw when the situation returned to normalcy.
However, there were still 6 Japanese soldiers stationed
behind the sand bags in front of the refugee camp on
each side of which were posted four City Government
policemen holding their rifles in the "ready" position.
Fortunately nothing untoward occurred.
An interpreter of the Japanese soldiers
told the inhabitants in the vicinity that the Japanese
were determined to recover the police right over the
Extra-Settlement roads areas as from September 9 and
should the British soldiers enter the area, the Japanese
would resort to force. Another interpreter said that
this was only a precautionary measure adopted for the
time being and that the Japanese soldiers would withdraw
after the anniversary of the September 18 Incident.
Yesterday morning the Japanese patrolled
Yu Yuen Road and other places but no Japanese soldiers
or puppet policemen were stationed at these places.
It could not be ascertained whether or not the Japanese
also patrolled Columbia Road.
page_data.zh:
昨日傍晚7时许，一辆载有约30名英军士兵的卡车疾驰至现场，并在难民营对面的人行道上架设了一挺机枪，枪口指向市政府阵地，从而导致气氛极为紧张。这种状态持续了一段时间，直到英军奉命撤离，局势才恢复正常。然而，仍有6名日军士兵驻守在难民营前的沙袋后方，难民营两侧各部署了4名手持步枪、处于“预备”射击姿态的市政府警察。幸未发生任何意外事件。

一名日军翻译告诉附近居民，日军决心自9月9日起收回越界筑路区域的警务权，若英军进入该区域，日军将诉诸武力。另一名翻译称，这仅是暂时采取的预防措施，待九一八事变纪念日过后，日军士兵将会撤离。

昨日上午，日军在愚园路等地进行了巡逻，但这些地方并未驻扎日军士兵或伪警察。目前尚无法确定日军是否也巡逻了哥伦比亚路（Columbia Road）。

CHINA PRESS
SEP 10 1939
Ta Tao Men
Filter Into
Western Area
Puppet Police Build
Sandbag Barricade On
Jessfield Road
Ta Tao Police, supported by uni-
formed Japanese, yesterday after-
noon built a sandbag barricade on
Jessfield Road, less than a block
from Bubbling Well police station,
and on outside Settlement-con-
trolled area. Along Bubbling Well
Road, they established a spaced
patrol, held by men armed with
rifles, and accompanied by Japan-
ese carrying pistols.
Uneasiness among western dis-
trict residents during the past two
weeks was heightened sharply
with the sudden appearance in
various areas of large numbers of
armed Ta Tao police, accompanied
by members of the Japanese Army
special service section, on outside
roads.
First appearing on Yu Yuen
Road in patrols of three, two
Chinese and a Japanese officer,
all marked with a white arm
band and armed with rifles or
revolvers, the Ta Tao police
"invasion" rapidly spread to
other sectors and a noticeable
increase of forces was effected
in the Columbia Road Area.
While infiltration throughout
the whole of the outside roads
district was consistently increas-
ed during the afternoon, without
undue alarm, the confirmed re-
port that more than a hundred
armed Ta Tao police were being
held in reserve in Fah Wah
Village led to consternation
among residents shortly before
this edition went to press.
Another late report, unable to
be confirmed at the last minute,
but coming from usually reliable
sources, declared that Japanese
troops had taken over a refugee
camp at 11 Jessfield Road, where
they were reported to be erecting
sandbag barricades and putting up
a strong redoubt.
It was learned late last evening
that the Shanghai Municipal Police
were not planning to take any im-
mediate action, but were watching
developments calmly.
（批：C.D. 3.6 / 10/10 / Asst. Liaison / 38 / 10/9）
